title: 7.1 A 212.5Gb/s DSP-Based PAM-4 Transceiver with 50dB Loss Compensation for Large AI System Interconnects in 4nm FinFET
problem: High-speed wireline links for AI/HPC systems (>200 Gb/s) face severe signal-integrity challenges—large package parasitics cause substantial channel loss (>50 dB) and reflections, requiring aggressive digital equalization that demands low jitter from the analog frontend while maintaining power efficiency.
motivation: Off-chip data transfer is a critical bottleneck for AI and HPC systems; 212.5 Gb/s interconnects with 50+ dB loss compensation enable efficient large-scale system communication.
method: Built in 4nm FinFET, the transceiver handles 212.5 Gb/s PAM-4 signals (2 bits encoded per voltage level) through three stages: a high-bandwidth, low-noise analog receiver operating at doubled signal rates to preserve full signal detail, digital equalization filters (FFE) with adjustable reflection-cancellation taps to undo distortion, and maximum-likelihood sequence detection (MLSD) that recovers data by determining the most probable original sequence through noise. These stages together compensate for over 50 dB of signal loss, enabling high-speed links in packaged AI systems.
key_novelty: By integrating analog-frontend bandwidth enhancement with digital equalization (FFE) and maximum-likelihood detection (MLSD), the transceiver achieves 50+ dB loss compensation at 212.5 Gb/s for packaged AI systems.
contributions: High-bandwidth analog frontend supporting 2x baud-rate signal handling for 212.5 Gb/s PAM-4
Extended FFE with floating taps for dynamic reflection-cancellation
MLSD receiver DSP for robust data recovery through severe loss
Practical demonstration achieving 2.5e-6 BER over 50+ dB loss channel
baselines: conventional transceiver designs without aggressive equalization
limitations: Power consumption, area, and latency metrics not specified in abstract; comparison with alternative equalization approaches not detailed.
primary_theme: High-speed DSP-based PAM-4 transceiver with aggressive loss compensation for AI system interconnects
